text: Marlo had watched the lights die from the jetty, and run the whole cliff path with every lantern off the ferry.
Twelve lanterns, in a ring around the cottage, an arm’s length apart.
At the edge of the ring, the dark stopped. It pressed against the light, the way the sea presses against a wall.
And in the dark, something smiled.
It could not come in. Not while the lanterns burned.
Marlo checked the oil. She did not say how much was left. She did not have to.
